That reddish blob is actually the terracotta plant pot, separate from the table which spans u61-190. I'm tracking the table legs by finding where the pixel columns bottom out - two legs reach v≈373 and 372, with another around v≈360.

For pose f99, I derive it from f98 by applying a turn of -3 degrees and a forward move of 0.75, giving a new heading and position around (1.048, 4.460).

Now I'm converting the leg-bottom pixel coordinates into ground-plane world coordinates using the depth/lateral projection formulas combined with the forward/right vectors from the current heading, computing the first leg lands around (3.25, 1.00) and starting the same calculation for the second leg.

Working through the second leg's projection, I get roughly (2.47, 1.00), matching the first leg's y-coordinate but offset by about 0.78 in x, consistent with two legs on the same rectangular edge. Trying the same math for a point near u181 gives (2.05, 0.61), which doesn't fit the rectangle formed by the other two legs, so I suspect that detection is off -- possibly a bad pixel read or partial occlusion -- and I need to re-examine the leg columns more carefully.

Scanning the pixel columns again, I can identify three distinct leg regions by where the intensity peaks: one near u~82, one near u~142, and one near u~181, with the tabletop visible between them. This still leaves the puzzle of only seeing three legs when a rectangular table viewed at this angle should show up to four, so I'm cross-referencing with earlier observations that placed front legs at (2.68, 2.13) and (2.81, 0.88), suggesting a leg pair spaced along the y-axis at x≈2.7-2.8, plus another observation near (2.28, 1.18).

Recomputing leg positions using a fresh set of pixel data gives (3.25, 1.00), (2.47, 1.00), and (2.05, 0.61) — but these don't line up with the earlier leg-pair estimate, so I suspect my dead-reckoned pose is drifting and needs correction.

To fix this, I'm using the known bearing to the plant to check my heading: computing the depth and lateral offset from my current pose to the plant center gives a predicted pixel column around u=253, which matches the observed plant pot center almost exactly, confirming my heading is accurate. But when I check the vertical position for the pot's base, my calculation puts it off the bottom of the frame, while the observed pot bottom edge sits at v=508, corresponding to a slightly closer depth than expected — meaning the visible base of the pot must be at a nearer point than my flat-ground assumption predicts.

Since the base circle's nearest edge should appear at the plant's center column in the image, but the pot silhouette shows the same max-v value across a stretch of columns rather than peaking at the center, this discrepancy points to either a wrong pot radius estimate or a pose error of roughly 0.36m in the y-direction. Given this inconsistency, I think the plant landmark alone isn't reliable enough for correction, so I should instead do a full resection using multiple landmarks — particularly the cabinet's floorline and front-face edges, which are already well-established — and check whether I have existing tooling in /work to run that resection properly.
